scope: Theorem 3.1 (One-sided marked Type II estimate) of the manuscript “The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors” (preprints/The-Poisson-Dirichlet-Law-for-Prime-Predecessors-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4b54d35506a19280), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix δ, C, D∗ > 0 and q ∈ (0, 1). Suppose Hm, Hn ≥ xδ and X = HmHn ≍ x. Let F satisfy |F(h)| ≤ 1 and F(ph) = F(h) for every prime in the groups (3.2). Let αm be supported on an arbitrary interval in [Hm, 2Hm], where it has the value αm = miv  1m prime − 1m rough V (W) log m  , |v| ≤ LC . Let βn be supported on rough integers in [Hn, 2Hn], with |βn| ≤ LC. If K is sufficiently large in terms of δ, C, D∗, q, then X m,n αmβnF(mn − 1)W(mn − 1) ≪ XL−D∗ . (3.5) The required lower bound on K is independent of the particular ai. The implicit constant and the threshold for x may depend on all the fixed parameters, including the ai.
